property_summary: The reference AccessControl contract's supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, but the mutant's supportsInterface always returns false for that interface ID.
For any interfaceId that should be supported according to the inherited chain (IAccessControl or IERC165), the reference returns true, but the mutant always returns false.

For any input, the reference c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, but the mutant always returns false, violating this for that specific interfaceId.

For any interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true exactly when interfaceId is type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, type(IERC165).interfaceId, or 0xffffffff; the mutant breakingly returns false for all inputs.

For any interfaceId, the reference C's supportsInterface must return the same boolean as the inherited AccessControl.supportsInterface (IAccessControl.id or super), but the mutant always returns false, so the rule 'returns bool' is violated for at least IAccessControl.id where reference returns true.

Reference C's supportsInterface returns true only for IAccessControl or IERC165 interface IDs; the buggy version always returns true, violating the general rule that supportsInterface must be consistent with the declared interfaces.
For any interface ID, c.supportsInterface(id) must return true iff id is the interface ID of IAccessControl or IERC165 or is supported by a parent; the bug breaks this by returning true for any id.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for both type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and type(IERC165).interfaceId (inherited via ERC165); the mutant returns false for IERC165, breaking the ERC165 contract.

For any bytes4 `interfaceId`, `supportsInterface` must return true for `type(IERC165).interfaceId` when the contract inherits ERC165; the mutant returns false for this interfaceId, violating ERC165 compliance.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if and only if it is a supported interface; since ERC165 is inherited, calling supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId) should return true, but the mutant returns false, thus the bug breaks that rule.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IERC165).interfaceId (inherited via ERC165); the buggy override returns false for that specific identifier.
supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId because the contract inherits ERC165, but the mutant returns false.
For any role and account, hasRole returns true if and only if the role was previously granted to the account and not revoked; the bug violates this by always returning false even after a valid grant.
For any PROPOSER_ROLE grant/revoke sequence where the role is eventually held, hasRole must return true; the bug always returns false even when the role is held.
After granting a role to an account via grantRole, hasRole(role, account) should return true; the bug always returns false.
For any role and account, after the role is granted and not revoked, hasRole must return true; the bug always returns false, so it fails even when the role is held.

For any role, if hasRole returns true, then the account must have been granted the role and not revoked; the bug returns false even after a valid grant, so the invariant is vacuously satisfied but the reference returns true after a grant.
For any role and account, hasRole returns true if and only if the role was previously granted to the account; the bug always returns true even for never-granted roles.
For any role and account, hasRole returns true if and only if the role was previously granted to the account; the bug always returns true even for never-granted roles.
hasRole returns true if and only if the role was previously granted; the mutant always returns true, so calling hasRole with a known non-granted role/sender pair returns true instead of false.

For every role, getRoleAdmin returns the correct admin role that was set via _setRoleAdmin or defaults to DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE; the buggy version always returns bytes32(0), which breaks this relationship for roles that have a non‑zero admin role.
For any non-DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE role that was set as its own admin via _setRoleAdmin(role, role), getRoleAdmin must return the role itself; the bug breaks this by always returning bytes32(0).
For any role that was set as its own admin using _setRoleAdmin(role, role), getRoleAdmin(role) must return the role itself; the bug always returns bytes32(0), violating this invariant.

The getRoleAdmin function must return the admin role stored in _roles. The reference always returns the stored admin role, while the mutant returns a constant non-zero value, which causes a mismatch for any call where the stored admin is not that constant.

For any role, getRoleAdmin(role) must return the admin role actually set via _setRoleAdmin in the constructor or subsequent updates; the mutant returns a fixed non-zero constant, violating this for roles whose real admin is not that constant.

For any role, getRoleAdmin(role) must equal the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (0) when the role has not been explicitly set; the mutant returns a constant non-zero value, violating this for the default admin role or any role with admin 0.
For any role, getRoleAdmin(role) must equal the stored admin role in _roles; the mutant returns a constant non-zero bytes32, so for at least the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE whose real admin is 0 it differs.

For any role, getRoleAdmin(role) returns the same value as the admin role set during construction via _setRoleAdmin; the mutant returns a constant non-zero value, which differs for roles whose admin is not that constant (e.g., DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE with admin 0x00).
